# BSON Update Expression

**Author: [Viraj Jasani](mailto:virajjasani007@gmail.com)**

This document describes how to create new functions that can support updating Phoenix BSON document field key-value pairs from top fields or nested fields and store the BSON document back to Phoenix BSON column. The update expression can be used to update the document partially or completely. Though using a UPSERT statement with a new BSON document for the same column would replace the whole document completely, hence the update expression is mostly used to partially update the documents.

If the update expression has to update any nested fields, first we need to access the nested field using the document path, and then make the update to the given BSON field.

## **Top-level Attributes:**

A field or an attribute is said to be top level if it is not embedded within another field.

## **Nested Attributes:**

A field or an attribute is said to be nested if it is embedded within another field. To access a nested field, you use dereference operators:

`[n]` — for list elements  
`.` (dot) — for document elements

## **Accessing list elements:**

The dereference operator for a list element is \[N\], where n is the element number. List elements are zero-based, so \[0\] represents the first element in the list, \[1\] represents the second, and so on. Here are some examples:

MyList\[0\]  
MyList\[12\]  
MyList\[5\]\[11\]

The element MyList\[5\] is itself a nested list. Therefore, MyList\[5\]\[11\] refers to the 12th element in that list.

## **Accessing document elements:**

The dereference operator for nested document elements is . (a dot). Use a dot as a separator between elements in a document:

MyMap.nestedField  
MyMap.nestedField.deeplyNestedField

The functions first retrieve the value of the field key by searching the field from top level of the BsonDocument. If the field key is not found, it follows `.` and `[]` notations for the nested fields.

## **Update expression Syntax:**

```javascript
update-expression :=
{
   "$SET": { <field1>: <value1>, <field2>: <value2>, .... },
   "$UNSET": { <field1>: null, <field2>: null, ... },
   "$ADD": { <field1>: <value1>, <field2>: <value2>, .... },
   "$DELETE_FROM_SET": { <field1>: <value1>, <field2>: <value2>, .... }
}
```

An update expression comprises one or more clauses, each beginning with a SET, REMOVE, ADD, or DELETE\_FROM\_SET keyword. User can include these clauses in any order within the update expression. Nonetheless, each action keyword can only occur once.

| Action | Definition |
| ----- | ----- |
| $SET | Use the SET action in an update expression to add one or more fields to a BSON Document. If any of these fields already exists, they are overwritten by the new values. To perform multiple SET actions, provide multiple fields key-value entries within the nested document under $SET field key. |
| $UNSET | Use the UNSET action in an update expression to unset or remove one or more fields from a BSON Document. To perform multiple REMOVE actions, provide multiple field key-value entries within the nested document under $UNSET field key.  |
| $ADD | Use the ADD action in an update expression to add a new field and its values to a BSON document. If the field already exists, the behavior of ADD depends on the field's data type: \* If the field is a number, and the value you are adding is also a number, the value is mathematically added to the existing field. \* If the field is a set, and the value you are adding is also a set, the value is appended to the existing set. Definition of path and value in the context of the expression: \* The path element is the document path to a field. The field must be either a Number or a set data type. \* The value element is a number that we want to add to the field (for Number data types), or a set to append to the field (for set types). |
| $DELETE\_FROM\_SET | Use the DELETE\_FROM\_SET action in an update expression to remove one or more elements from a set. To perform multiple DELETE\_FROM\_SET actions, provide multiple field key-value entries within the nested document under $DELETE\_FROM\_SET field key. Definition of path and subset in the context of the expression: \* The path element is the document path to a field. The field must be a set data type. \* The subset is one or more elements that you want to delete from the given path. Subset must be of set type. |

## **Function Grammar:**

**Name:** `BSON_UPDATE_EXPRESSION`

**Arguments:**

|  | Expression | DataType |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Column Value | BSON |
| 2 | Update Expression | BSON |

**Definition:** The function retrieves the BSON document for the given column, and performs updates to top-level and/or nested/complex fields of the document based on the update expression provided as part of the input. The value placeholders in the update expression are provided as third argument i.e. expression values. The expression values is the JSON string representing the BSON document for the expression values.

**Return Type:** BSON

**JDBC API:**

Use Class BsonUpdateExpressionUtil to build BsonDocument for Update Expression.

* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#setFieldValues  
* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#unsetFiels  
* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#addFielValues  
* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#deleteFieldValues  
* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#renameFields  
* BsonUpdateExpressionUtil\#mulFieldValues

PhoenixPreparedStatement to provide extended API to set BsonDocument for parameterized values:

* PhoenixPreparedStatement\#setBson

**SQLLine Examples:**

* This example will set the top-level attribute “Title” with value “Cycle\_1234\_new” and “Id” with numeric value 12345\.   
* It will also remove top-level attributes: "IdS" and "Id2".   
* It will add numeric value 10 to top-level attribute "AddedId" and subtract numeric value 12345 from nested attribute "NestedMap1.NestedMap2.Id".  
* It will add string values "xyz5@\_rear.jpg" and "1235@\_rear.jpg" to existing Set defined at top-level attribute "Pictures". This operation will add the string values to the existing set only if the existing set of string values do not contain these values.  
* It will remove string values "Book 1011 Title" and "Book 1010 Title" from the set represented by nested-attribute "NestedList1\[2\]\[1\].TitleSet2". The operation will remove the string values from the existing set only if the existing set of string values contain these values already.

```javascript
UPSERT INTO TABLE_NAME VALUES (?,?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE COL = CASE WHEN BSON_CONDITION_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$EXPR":"Picture = $PictureVal AND NestedMap1.NestedMap2.NList[1] < $NList001","$VAL":{"$NList001":12.22,"$PictureVal":"Blue"}}') THEN BSON_UPDATE_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$SET":{"Title":"Cycle_1234_new","Id":12345},"$UNSET":{"IdS":null,"Id2":null},"$ADD":{"AddedId":10,"NestedMap1.NestedMap2.Id":-12345,"Pictures":{"$set":["xyz5@_rear.jpg","1235@_rear.jpg"]}},"$DELETE_FROM_SET":{"NestedList1[2][1].TitleSet2":{"$set":["Book 1011 Title","Book 1010 Title"]}}}') ELSE COL END
```

```javascript
UPSERT INTO TABLE_NAME VALUES (?,?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE COL = CASE WHEN BSON_CONDITION_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$EXPR": "PictureBinarySet = $PictureBinarySet AND NestedMap1.NestedMap2.NList[1] < $NList001", "$VAL": {"$NList001": 12.22, "$PictureBinarySet": {"$set": [{"$binary": {"base64": "MTIzX3JlYXIuanBn", "subType": "00"}}, {"$binary": {"base64": "MTIzYWJjX3JlYXIuanBn", "subType": "00"}}, {"$binary": {"base64": "eHl6X3JlYXIuanBn", "subType": "00"}}, {"$binary": {"base64": "eHl6YWJjX3JlYXIuanBn", "subType": "00"}}, {"$binary": {"base64": "MTIzX2Zyb250LmpwZw==", "subType": "00"}}, {"$binary": {"base64": "eHl6X2Zyb250LmpwZw==", "subType": "00"}}]}}}') THEN BSON_UPDATE_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$SET": {"Title": "Cycle_1234_new", "Id": 12345, "NestedMap1.ColorList": ["Black", {"$binary": {"base64": "V2hpdGU=", "subType": "00"}}, "Silver"]}, "$UNSET": {"IdS": null, "Id2": null, "NestedMap1.Title": null}, "$ADD": {"AddedId": 10, "NestedMap1.AddedId": 10, "NestedMap1.NestedMap2.Id": -12345, "NestedList12[2][0]": {"$set": ["xyz01234", "abc01234"]}, "Pictures": {"$set": ["xyz5@_rear.jpg", "1235@_rear.jpg"]}}, "$DELETE_FROM_SET": {"NestedMap1.NSet1": {"$set": [-6830.5555, -48695]}, "NestedList1[2][1].TitleSet2": {"$set": ["Book 1011 Title", "Book 1010 Title"]}}}') ELSE COL END
```

**Document style Example:**

```javascript
UPSERT INTO TABLE_NAME VALUES (?,?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE COL = CASE WHEN BSON_CONDITION_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$and":[{"NestedMap1.ISBN":{"$exists":true}},{"NestedMap1.NList1[3]":{"$exists":false}}]}') THEN BSON_UPDATE_EXPRESSION(COL, '{"$SET":{"Title":"Cycle_1234_new","Id":12345},"$UNSET":{"IdS":null,"Id2":null},"ADD":{"AddedId":10,"NestedMap1.NestedMap2.Id":-12345,"Pictures":{"$set":["xyz5@_rear.jpg","1235@_rear.jpg"]}},"DELETE":{"NestedList1[2][1].TitleSet2":{"$set":["Book 1011 Title","Book 1010 Title"]}}}') ELSE COL END
```
